reading.title: Extract from a majority agreement on a job protection plan
paragraphs: Article 4 - Internal redeployment

4.1 Before any dismissal is notified, the Company shall seek to redeploy each employee whose position is eliminated to an available position within the Company or within the other companies of the Group located in France, in the same job category or, failing that, in an equivalent position at an equivalent level of pay.

4.2 Subject to the employee's express consent, redeployment to a lower-graded position may also be offered. In that event, a temporary differential allowance shall be paid in accordance with Appendix 4.

4.3 Redeployment offers shall be made in writing and shall specify the job title, the employing entity, the place of work, the remuneration and the grade. The employee shall have twenty-one calendar days from receipt of the offer in which to reply. Failure to reply within that period shall be deemed a refusal. A refusal shall not constitute misconduct and shall be without prejudice to the employee's entitlements under this Agreement.
Article 5 - Redeployment leave

5.1 Any employee who is given notice of dismissal on economic grounds shall be offered redeployment leave of nine months, extended to twelve months for employees aged fifty or over or recognised as disabled workers.

5.2 Throughout the leave, the employee shall be released from work in order to devote himself or herself to the search for new employment, with the support of the redeployment unit. For the portion of the leave exceeding the notice period, the employee shall receive a monthly allowance equal to 75% of his or her average gross remuneration.
5.3 An employee who finds new employment before the end of the leave shall receive a lump sum equal to half of the allowances outstanding at the date of departure.

reading.title: Memo to a US board: why the French timeline cannot be compressed
paragraphs: To: Board of Directors, Hartwell Industries Inc. From: Hélène Marchand, Interim HR Director, Hartwell France SAS. Re: Project Cedar - French timeline

You have asked whether the 118 position eliminations planned at the Angers plant could be completed within the sixty days we would allow for a WARN notice at home. The short answer is no, and I would advise against trying.

In France, a company of our size that contemplates ten or more dismissals within thirty days must draw up a job protection plan and consult its works council on both the business rationale and the plan itself. With between 100 and 249 dismissals, the council has three months to give its opinion. That period is set by statute; we can agree a different one with the unions, but we cannot impose a shorter one.

In parallel, we will try to negotiate the plan with the unions. If we reach a majority agreement, the labor authority has fifteen days to validate it. If we do not, we file a unilateral plan, which the authority reviews more closely and has twenty-one days to approve. No termination letter may go out before that decision; any that did would be void.

Realistically, then: announcement in early March, consultation through early June, the authority's decision by the end of June, first letters in July. Employees then work out their notice or enter redeployment leave, so most will remain on payroll into next year. Employee representatives need separate clearance from the labor inspector, which adds roughly two months for those individuals.

Two things would lengthen this further: an incomplete information package, which invites the authority to step in and hands the council an argument in court, and a legal challenge to the plan itself. Both are avoided by preparation, not by speed. I would therefore ask the Board to approve the timeline in Appendix A and to book the restructuring charge on that basis.

reading.title: Letter to the labour administration requesting validation of an agreement
paragraphs: Courtesy translation for Group Legal - the original was filed in French.

To the Regional Director for the Economy, Employment, Labour and Solidarity. Re: Request for validation of the majority collective agreement on the job protection plan - Brennard Logistics France SAS, Orléans establishment.
Dear Sir or Madam,

Further to the notification of our project sent to your office on 12 February, we hereby submit for validation the collective agreement signed on 18 April with two representative trade unions which together obtained 63% of the votes cast in the first round of the most recent workplace elections.

The agreement provides for the elimination of 74 positions following the closure of the Orléans cross-docking platform. It determines the content of the job protection plan, the timetable for dismissals, the job categories concerned, the weighting and scope of the selection criteria, and the arrangements for implementing the training and redeployment measures.

The works council was informed and consulted at five meetings held between 14 February and 11 April and delivered its opinion at the last of those meetings. The minutes of the meetings, the report of the expert appointed by the council and the Company's replies to your observations of 21 March are enclosed.
We remain at your disposal for any further information you may require during the examination period and would be grateful if you would acknowledge receipt of this application.
Yours faithfully,
Antoine Leclercq, Chairman

reading.title: An offer of internal redeployment
paragraphs: Dear Mr Delmas,
Offer of internal redeployment

As you know, the reorganisation project presented to the works council provides for the elimination of your position of Maintenance Technician at our Roubaix site. In accordance with the job protection plan, we have looked for available positions within the company and the group's other French entities that match your skills, and we are pleased to make you the following offer.

Position: Maintenance Technician, automated lines. Employer: Oriel Packaging France SAS. Location: Chalon-sur-Saône plant. Contract: permanent, full-time. Grade: unchanged. Basic salary: EUR 2,640 gross per month, plus shift allowance.

Should you accept, you would be entitled to the relocation assistance set out in the plan: removal costs, a settling-in allowance and two paid trips to visit the area with your family. You would also have a six-week adaptation period, during which you could change your mind and return to the measures of the plan without losing any entitlement.

You have twenty-one calendar days from receipt of this letter to let us know your decision, using the enclosed reply form. If we have not heard from you by then, we will take it that you have declined. Please be assured that declining this offer will not affect your rights under the plan in any way.
Sophie Renard in the HR team would be glad to go through the offer with you and can be reached on extension 4127.
Yours sincerely,
Marc Vasseur, Site HR Manager

writing.title: Updating head office on the negotiation
writing.brief: You are the interim HR Director of a French subsidiary. After the fourth negotiation meeting on the redundancy plan, write to the Group HR Director, Fiona Aldridge: what has been agreed, what is still blocking, the recommendation you are making, its cost, the status of the consultation and the decision you need from her.
writing.brief_fr: Vous êtes DRH de transition d'une filiale française. Après la quatrième réunion de négociation du plan, écrivez à la DRH groupe, Fiona Aldridge : ce qui est acquis, le point de blocage, votre recommandation et son coût, l'état de la consultation et la décision que vous attendez d'elle.

gaps.text: We have now reached agreement ___ on the redeployment measures and on the length of redeployment leave.
gaps.explain_fr: « Agreement in principle » = accord de principe. Sans article devant « agreement » dans l'expression « to reach agreement ».

gaps.text: The main ___ remains the enhanced severance.
gaps.explain_fr: « Sticking point » = point de blocage. Évitez le calque « blocking point ».

gaps.text: The unions are asking for one month's pay per year of service, ___ our mandate stops at 0.6.
gaps.explain_fr: « Whereas » oppose deux faits dans la même phrase, sans la lourdeur de « on the contrary » ou « but on the other hand ».

gaps.text: ___, we would have to fall back on a unilateral plan.
gaps.explain_fr: « Failing that » = à défaut. Formule concise, très utile pour présenter le scénario de repli.

gaps.text: The consultation of the works council is ___, and no further meetings have been requested.
gaps.explain_fr: « On track » = conforme au calendrier prévu. « In time » ou « in the delays » seraient fautifs.

gaps.text: The council is ___ deliver its opinion on 12 June.
gaps.explain_fr: « To be due to » + verbe = devoir (selon le calendrier prévu). Plus naturel que « must » ou « will have to ».

writing.model:
Subject: Project Atlas - negotiation update after round four

Dear Fiona,

A quick update following yesterday's fourth negotiation meeting with the unions.

We have now reached agreement in principle on the redeployment measures and on the length of redeployment leave. The main sticking point remains the enhanced severance: the unions are asking for one month's pay per year of service, whereas our mandate stops at 0.6.

Two of the three unions have indicated that they would be prepared to sign at 0.8, which would give us a majority agreement. Failing that, we would have to fall back on a unilateral plan, with a closer review by the labour authority and a higher risk of litigation.

I would therefore recommend that we move to 0.8. The additional cost is estimated at EUR 640,000, which is still within the provision.

The consultation of the works council is on track, and the council is due to deliver its opinion on 12 June.

Could you let me know by Thursday whether we have a mandate to close on that basis? I am happy to talk it through beforehand if that would help.

Kind regards,
Hélène
writing.model_us:
Subject: Project Atlas - negotiation update after round four

Hi Fiona,

A quick update following yesterday's fourth negotiation meeting with the unions.

We have now reached agreement in principle on the redeployment measures and on the length of redeployment leave. The main sticking point is still the enhanced severance: the unions are asking for one month of pay per year of service, while our mandate stops at 0.6.

Two of the three unions have indicated that they would be prepared to sign at 0.8, which would give us a majority agreement. Otherwise, we would have to fall back on a unilateral plan, with a closer review by the labor authority and a higher risk of litigation.

I therefore recommend that we move to 0.8. The additional cost is estimated at EUR 640,000, which is still within the reserve.

The works council consultation is on track, and the council is scheduled to deliver its opinion on June 12.

Could you let me know by Thursday whether we have a mandate to close on that basis? I'm happy to talk it through beforehand if that would help.

Best regards,

commentary.quote: A quick update following yesterday's fourth negotiation meeting
commentary.note_fr: Entrée en matière directe, sans phrase verbale : usage courant dans un e-mail entre collègues. « Following » suffit ; « following to » est fautif.

commentary.quote: whereas our mandate stops at 0.6
commentary.note_fr: « Mandate » désigne ici l'autorisation donnée par le siège au négociateur. Le chiffre est donné sans détour : un siège veut l'écart exact.

commentary.quote: Failing that, we would have to fall back on a unilateral plan
commentary.note_fr: Le scénario de repli est présenté au conditionnel, avec ses deux inconvénients. « To fall back on » = se rabattre sur.

commentary.quote: I would therefore recommend that we move to 0.8
commentary.note_fr: La recommandation est explicite et tient en une phrase. « I would recommend that we » + base verbale : pas de « to » après « recommend ».

commentary.quote: Could you let me know by Thursday whether we have a mandate to close on that basis?
commentary.note_fr: La demande de décision est datée et fermée : la destinataire sait exactement ce qu'on attend d'elle. « To close » = conclure (un accord).

checklist: Have I separated what is agreed from what is still open?
Have I given the exact figures (demand, mandate, proposal, cost)?
Have I explained the fallback and its risks in one sentence?
Is my recommendation stated clearly, in my own name?
Have I asked for a decision by a specific date?

writing.title: Minutes of a works council consultation meeting
writing.brief: Write the English version, for head office, of the extract of the minutes of the first works council meeting on the proposed reorganisation of the Angers plant: opening, presentation of the project, the union's challenge, the appointment of the expert, the date of the next meeting.
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez, pour le siège, la version anglaise de l'extrait du procès-verbal de la première réunion du CSE sur le projet de réorganisation de l'usine d'Angers : ouverture, présentation du projet, contestation syndicale, désignation de l'expert, date de la prochaine réunion.

gaps.text: The Chair ___ members that this was the first meeting of the consultation procedure.
gaps.explain_fr: « To remind someone that » = rappeler à quelqu'un que. « To recall » signifie se souvenir et ne prend pas de complément de personne.

gaps.text: The project would ___ the elimination of 118 positions.
gaps.explain_fr: « To entail » = entraîner, impliquer. Notez le conditionnel « would » : le projet n'est pas encore décidé.

gaps.text: Mr Garnier, ___ the majority union, challenged the figures on the order book.
gaps.explain_fr: « On behalf of » = au nom de, pour le compte de. « In the name of » est réservé aux invocations solennelles.

gaps.text: Management ___ to provide the forecasts within one week.
gaps.explain_fr: « To undertake to do » = s'engager à faire, verbe type des procès-verbaux. Prétérit irrégulier : undertook.

gaps.text: The council voted ___ to appoint the firm Axiome Conseil as its expert.
gaps.explain_fr: « Unanimously » = à l'unanimité. L'adverbe se place naturellement après « voted ».
« To adjourn a meeting » = lever la séance. « The meeting was closed » est possible ; « finished » ou « ended » manquent de tenue.

writing.model:
Hartwell France SAS - Works Council
Minutes of the extraordinary meeting of 14 March (extract)

Item 1 - Information and consultation on the proposed reorganisation of the Angers plant

The Chair opened the meeting at 9.30 a.m. and reminded members that this was the first meeting of the consultation procedure. She stressed that the project was at the proposal stage and that no decision would be taken until the council had delivered its opinion.

Management presented the economic rationale for the project, which would entail the elimination of 118 positions. Mr Garnier, on behalf of the majority union, challenged the figures on the order book and asked for the detailed forecasts by product line. Management undertook to provide them within one week.

The council voted unanimously to appoint the firm Axiome Conseil as its expert. The Secretary pointed out that the expert's report would be needed before any discussion of the selection criteria.

It was agreed that the second meeting would be held on 4 April. The meeting was adjourned at 12.45 p.m.

commentary.quote: She stressed that the project was at the proposal stage
commentary.note_fr: Discours rapporté au passé : « stressed that ... was ». Variez les verbes introducteurs : stressed, pointed out, asked, replied, undertook.

commentary.quote: no decision would be taken until the council had delivered its opinion
commentary.note_fr: Concordance des temps : « will be taken » devient « would be taken », « has delivered » devient « had delivered ». Phrase juridiquement importante à faire figurer au procès-verbal.

commentary.quote: challenged the figures on the order book
commentary.note_fr: « To challenge » = contester ; plus neutre que « to criticise » et moins fort que « to reject ». « Order book » = carnet de commandes.

commentary.quote: It was agreed that the second meeting would be held on 4 April
commentary.note_fr: Tournure impersonnelle passive, caractéristique des procès-verbaux : elle évite de dire qui a proposé quoi.

commentary.quote: The council voted unanimously to appoint
commentary.note_fr: « To vote to do something » : pas de « for » devant l'infinitif. « To appoint an expert » = désigner un expert.

checklist: Are the minutes written in the past tense, in reported speech?
Have I named who said what, by function rather than by first name?
Does the text make clear that the project is only a proposal?
Are decisions and undertakings recorded with their dates?
Have I kept my own opinions and adjectives out of it?

Management presented ...

writing.title: Talking points for line managers on announcement day
writing.brief: The proposal to reorganise the Angers plant (118 positions) is being presented to the works council this morning. Write the talking points that line managers will use with their teams in the afternoon: short, honest and usable aloud.
writing.brief_fr: Le projet de réorganisation de l'usine d'Angers (118 postes) est présenté ce matin au CSE. Rédigez les éléments de langage que les managers de proximité utiliseront l'après-midi avec leurs équipes : brefs, honnêtes et utilisables à l'oral.
outline: What was presented this morning, and the fact that it is only a proposal
Nobody knows yet who is affected: positions, not people
What the company commits to: redeployment, volunteers, support
What managers must not do; where to send questions
The attitude expected of managers this week
writing.model:
Talking points for line managers - Thursday 14 March

This morning the company presented to the works council a proposal to reorganise the Angers plant, which could lead to the loss of 118 positions. Please be clear with your teams that this is a proposal: nothing will be decided until the consultation is complete, which we expect to be in June at the earliest.

At this stage nobody can say which individuals would be affected. The plan identifies positions, not people, and the selection criteria are set by law and have still to be discussed with the employee representatives. If you are asked 'Is it me?', the honest answer is that we do not know yet, and that no one will receive a letter before the summer.

What we can say is that the company will do everything it reasonably can to keep compulsory departures to a minimum: internal redeployment first, then voluntary departures, with training and outplacement support for everyone concerned.

Please do not speculate, make promises or comment on individual cases, however well meant. Note any question you cannot answer and pass it to HR the same day; we will come back to your team within forty-eight hours. Above all, stay visible. People will remember how they were treated this week long after they have forgotten the figures.

commentary.quote: which could lead to the loss of 118 positions
commentary.note_fr: « Could » et non « will » : tant que la consultation n'est pas achevée, tout s'exprime au conditionnel. C'est une exigence juridique autant qu'une précaution de langage.

commentary.quote: The plan identifies positions, not people
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte, facile à retenir et à répéter : c'est le message central pour les équipes. L'opposition « positions / people » fait tout le travail.

commentary.quote: the honest answer is that we do not know yet
commentary.note_fr: On donne au manager la réponse mot pour mot à la question la plus difficile. « The honest answer is » annonce une vérité inconfortable sans brutalité.

commentary.quote: Please do not speculate, make promises or comment on individual cases, however well meant
commentary.note_fr: Trois interdits en une phrase, adoucis par « please » et « however well meant » (même avec les meilleures intentions).

commentary.quote: Above all, stay visible.
commentary.note_fr: Impératif bref en fin de note : le changement de rythme signale l'essentiel. « To stay visible » = rester présent sur le terrain.

checklist: Could a manager read each sentence aloud without stumbling?
Have I used 'proposal', 'could' and 'would' rather than 'decision' and 'will'?
Have I given a ready-made answer to the hardest question?
Have I said clearly what managers must not do?
Do managers know where to send questions and how quickly they will get answers?
phrasebank: Please be clear with your teams that this is a proposal.
Nothing will be decided until the consultation is complete.
At this stage nobody can say which individuals would be affected.
The honest answer is that we do not know yet.
What we can say is that ...
The company will do everything it reasonably can to ...
Note any question you cannot answer and pass it to HR the same day.

writing.title: A progress report on redeployment for the monitoring committee
writing.brief: Six months after the first departures, write the summary section of the report sent to group HR ahead of the monitoring committee: results of the redeployment unit, the people still without a solution, action taken, and the request about the unused training budget.
writing.brief_fr: Six mois après les premiers départs, rédigez la synthèse du rapport adressé à la DRH groupe avant la commission de suivi : résultats de la cellule de reclassement, personnes encore sans solution, actions engagées et demande relative au budget de formation non consommé.
outline: Headline figures: how many people have joined the unit and how many have a lasting solution
Breakdown of solutions: jobs, retraining, business start-ups, early retirement
Who is still looking for work, and why
What the outplacement firm is doing for that group
Budget position and the committee's request; what you need from the Group
writing.model:
Redeployment progress at 30 November

Six months after the first departures, 96 of the 118 employees covered by the plan have joined the redeployment unit, and 61 of them now have what the plan defines as a lasting solution. Of these, 38 have found a permanent job or a fixed-term contract of six months or more, 14 are on long retraining courses and 9 have set up their own business. A further 12 opted for early retirement and are no longer being followed.

That leaves 23 people still looking for work. Most are operators over fifty with long service and qualifications that do not transfer easily; several are also reluctant to travel more than thirty kilometres. The outplacement firm has stepped up its efforts for this group, with weekly one-to-one sessions and direct approaches to employers in the area, and two local companies have agreed to offer trial periods in January.

Spending stands at 71% of the training budget. Given the profile of those remaining, the monitoring committee has asked that the unused balance be ring-fenced for them rather than released. We support that request and would be grateful for the Group's agreement before the committee's next meeting on 15 December.

commentary.quote: 96 of the 118 employees covered by the plan have joined the redeployment unit
commentary.note_fr: Le chiffre clé arrive dès la première phrase, rapporté au total. « Covered by the plan » = entrant dans le champ du plan.

commentary.quote: Of these, 38 have found a permanent job
commentary.note_fr: « Of these » introduit la ventilation sans répéter le nom. Present perfect, car le résultat vaut à la date du rapport.

commentary.quote: That leaves 23 people still looking for work.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase charnière très naturelle pour passer aux cas non résolus. On écrit « people », pas « persons » ni « cases ».

commentary.quote: has stepped up its efforts for this group
commentary.note_fr: « To step up » = intensifier. Verbe à particule de registre courant, parfaitement admis dans un rapport.

commentary.quote: has asked that the unused balance be ring-fenced for them rather than released
commentary.note_fr: Subjonctif après « ask that » (« be ring-fenced »). « To ring-fence » = sanctuariser un budget ; aux États-Unis on dirait plutôt « to set aside » ou « to earmark ».

commentary.quote: would be grateful for the Group's agreement before the committee's next meeting
commentary.note_fr: La demande est polie mais assortie d'une échéance : le lecteur sait quelle décision prendre et pour quand.

checklist: Do my figures add up, and is each one related to a total?
Have I moved from the overall picture to the difficult cases?
Have I explained why the remaining group is hard to place, without blaming anyone?
Have I described concrete action rather than good intentions?
Does the paragraph end with a clear request and a date?
phrasebank: Six months after the first departures, ...
... now have what the plan defines as a lasting solution.
Of these, ... have found ..., ... are on ... and ... have set up ...
That leaves ... people still looking for work.
The outplacement firm has stepped up its efforts for this group.
Spending stands at ...% of the budget.
We support that request and would be grateful for the Group's agreement before ...

writing.title: A note comparing a negotiated plan with a unilateral one
writing.brief: Write a one-page note for the Executive Committee of an international group comparing the two routes available in France for a job protection plan - majority agreement or unilateral document - and recommending one. Cover the administrative review, risk, time and cost.
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez pour le comité exécutif d'un groupe international une note d'une page comparant les deux voies possibles en France pour un PSE - accord majoritaire ou document unilatéral - et recommandant l'une d'elles. Traitez le contrôle de l'administration, le risque, les délais et le coût.
outline: Purpose of the note
The two routes, defined in plain English
How the labour authority reviews each of them
Risk, time and cost compared
Recommendation and the decision requested
writing.model:
Note for the Executive Committee
Project Cedar: negotiated agreement or unilateral plan?

Purpose
French law gives us two ways of putting a job protection plan in place. This note compares them and recommends which to pursue.

The two routes
Under the first, we negotiate the plan with the representative unions and sign a majority agreement, that is, one signed by unions which together won more than half of the votes at the last workplace elections. Under the second, management draws up the plan on its own, in what is known as a unilateral document, after consulting the works council. The two can be combined: a partial agreement on some topics, completed by a unilateral document on the rest.

How the authority reviews them
In both cases the plan must be cleared by the regional labour authority before any dismissal is notified. An agreement is validated within fifteen days, and the authority looks mainly at whether it was properly signed and whether the consultation was regular. A unilateral document is approved within twenty-one days after a fuller review, including whether the measures are proportionate to the resources of the group as a whole.

Risk, time and cost
An agreement is considerably harder to challenge in court, and unions that have signed it rarely campaign against it. It also allows us to tailor certain rules, such as the scope within which the selection criteria apply. The price is time at the table and, in all likelihood, a higher package: we estimate the premium at 10 to 15% of the plan budget. A unilateral plan keeps us in control of the content, but it exposes the company to closer scrutiny, a more hostile climate on site and a greater risk of annulment.

Recommendation
We recommend opening negotiations with a view to a majority agreement, while preparing a unilateral document in parallel as a fallback. We would ask the Committee to approve a negotiating mandate on that basis.

commentary.quote: This note compares them and recommends which to pursue.
commentary.note_fr: L'objet de la note tient en une phrase et annonce qu'elle conclut par une recommandation : c'est ce qu'attend un comité exécutif.

commentary.quote: that is, one signed by unions which together won more than half of the votes
commentary.note_fr: La notion française est glosée au fil de la phrase grâce à « that is, » : pas de parenthèse en français, pas de jargon.

commentary.quote: in what is known as a unilateral document
commentary.note_fr: « What is known as » introduit le terme technique tout en signalant qu'il s'agit d'une appellation consacrée.

commentary.quote: The price is time at the table and, in all likelihood, a higher package
commentary.note_fr: Formulation franche et imagée : « the price is » annonce la contrepartie ; « in all likelihood » nuance sans affaiblir.

commentary.quote: A unilateral plan keeps us in control of the content, but it exposes the company to closer scrutiny
commentary.note_fr: Structure avantage / inconvénient en une phrase. « Scrutiny » = examen attentif, contrôle.

commentary.quote: while preparing a unilateral document in parallel as a fallback
commentary.note_fr: La recommandation intègre le plan B : « a fallback » = solution de repli. Un comité exécutif apprécie qu'on ne mise pas tout sur une seule issue.

checklist: Could a reader with no knowledge of French law follow every sentence?
Have I explained each French notion the first time it appears?
Have I compared the two routes on the same points: review, risk, time, cost?
Are the legal statements general and accurate, with no article numbers?
Is the recommendation unambiguous, with a fallback?
Have I said what decision I need from the Committee?
phrasebank: French law gives us two ways of ...
Under the first, ... Under the second, ...
... in what is known as a unilateral document.
In both cases the plan must be cleared by the labour authority before ...
The price is ...
... exposes the company to closer scrutiny and a greater risk of ...
We recommend ..., while preparing ... in parallel as a fallback.
We would ask the Committee to approve a negotiating mandate on that basis.

writing.title: Email to a US general counsel: what we can and cannot do on timing
writing.brief: After a call with Dan Kessler, General Counsel of the US parent, who wanted the French plan completed in thirty days, write the follow-up email: explain why that is impossible, then set out what can be done to keep the timetable as short as the law allows, and give a realistic target.
writing.brief_fr: Après un appel avec Dan Kessler, directeur juridique de la maison mère américaine, qui voulait boucler le plan français en trente jours, rédigez l'e-mail de suivi : expliquez pourquoi c'est impossible, puis ce qui peut être fait pour tenir le calendrier le plus court permis par la loi, et donnez un objectif réaliste.
outline: Thank him and state the purpose of the email
Why thirty days is not possible: consultation period, approval, consequence of acting early
What can be done to save time (four levers)
A realistic target and why it is defensible
Offer to present it to the board
writing.model:
Subject: Project Cedar - what we can and cannot do on timing

Dear Dan,

Thank you for your time on Tuesday. As promised, here is a written summary of where we stand on the timetable, and of what we can do to keep it as short as the law allows.

I am afraid a thirty-day process is not an option in France. Because we are proposing more than a hundred redundancies, the works council has three months in which to give its opinion, and the labour authority then has up to twenty-one days to approve the plan. Any dismissal notified before that approval would be void, and the employees concerned could claim reinstatement.

That said, there is a good deal we can do to avoid losing time:

- Prepare thoroughly. Most delays come from incomplete information, which gives the council grounds to ask the labour authority to step in and, later, to challenge the plan. I would rather announce two weeks later with a complete file.
- Sign a method agreement. Agreeing the dates of all the meetings with the unions at the outset makes the three months a ceiling rather than a starting point.
- Open a voluntary phase early. Volunteers can leave as soon as the plan is approved, which brings part of the savings forward.
- Negotiate. A majority agreement is cleared in fifteen days rather than twenty-one and is far less likely to be challenged.

On that basis, a realistic target is an announcement on 3 March and first departures in early July. I appreciate this is not the answer you were hoping for, but it is one we can defend, and it protects the group against the far greater cost of a plan struck down in court.

I would be glad to walk the board through this on the 20th if that would be useful.

Kind regards,
Hélène Marchand
Interim HR Director, Hartwell France

commentary.quote: I am afraid a thirty-day process is not an option in France.
commentary.note_fr: Le refus est net mais adouci par « I am afraid ». « Is not an option » ferme la porte sans agressivité ; inutile d'écrire « impossible ».

commentary.quote: Any dismissal notified before that approval would be void
commentary.note_fr: La conséquence juridique est énoncée simplement, au conditionnel. « Void » = nul : mot bref, que tout juriste américain comprend.

commentary.quote: That said, there is a good deal we can do to avoid losing time:
commentary.note_fr: « That said » fait pivoter le message du non vers les solutions : indispensable pour ne pas laisser le lecteur sur un refus. « A good deal » = beaucoup (registre britannique soigné).

commentary.quote: makes the three months a ceiling rather than a starting point
commentary.note_fr: Image parlante pour un non-spécialiste. « A ceiling » = un plafond ; « rather than » évite une seconde phrase.

commentary.quote: I appreciate this is not the answer you were hoping for, but it is one we can defend
commentary.note_fr: « I appreciate » = je mesure bien que. On reconnaît la déception du lecteur avant de justifier sa position : concession, puis argument.

commentary.quote: I would be glad to walk the board through this
commentary.note_fr: « To walk someone through something » = expliquer pas à pas. Offre de service qui clôt l'e-mail sur une note constructive.

checklist: Have I said no clearly, once, without apologising at length?
Have I given the legal reason in two or three sentences, with no article numbers?
Have I moved quickly from the constraint to what can be done?
Is each lever expressed as an action with its benefit?
Have I given dates the reader can take to the board?
Is the tone that of an adviser, neither defensive nor lecturing?
phrasebank: As promised, here is a written summary of where we stand on ...
I am afraid ... is not an option in France.
Any dismissal notified before that approval would be void.
That said, there is a good deal we can do to ...
I would rather ... than ...
On that basis, a realistic target is ...
I appreciate this is not the answer you were hoping for, but it is one we can defend.
I would be glad to walk the board through this.

dialogues.title: Thirty days? A call with the US general counsel
dialogues.context: Dan, General Counsel of a US industrial group, calls Hélène, interim HR Director of the French subsidiary. The board wants the 118 job cuts at the Angers plant completed in thirty days.
dialogues.context_fr: Dan, directeur juridique d'un groupe industriel américain, appelle Hélène, DRH de transition de la filiale française. Le conseil d'administration veut boucler en trente jours les 118 suppressions de postes de l'usine d'Angers.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: Hélène, I'll be straight with you. The board wants Angers wrapped up in thirty days. We did Ohio in sixty, WARN notice included.
lines.note_fr: « I'll be straight with you » = je vais être franc. « To wrap something up » = boucler. La référence américaine est le préavis WARN de soixante jours.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I understand the pressure, Dan, and I'd love to give you thirty days. But in France the clock isn't ours to set. With this many jobs, the works council gets three months to give its opinion.
lines.note_fr: « The clock isn't ours to set » : façon imagée de dire que le délai est légal. On reconnaît d'abord la contrainte de l'autre avant de dire non.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: Three months to give an opinion? Can they block it?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: No, they can't veto it. But if we skip the process or rush it, the plan gets thrown out, and every termination with it.
lines.note_fr: « To get thrown out » = être annulé, rejeté (par un juge). « To skip » = sauter une étape.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: Okay. So who actually signs off on this thing?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: The regional labor authority. They either validate an agreement we've signed with the unions, or approve a plan we've drawn up ourselves. Nothing goes out until they do.
lines.note_fr: « Either ... or » présente clairement les deux voies : accord majoritaire validé, ou document unilatéral homologué.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: And if we just pay people more? Double the severance, get releases, and move on?
lines.note_fr: « Release » : renonciation à recours signée en échange de l'indemnité, réflexe américain.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Money helps at the table, but it doesn't buy time. And a release signed before termination wouldn't hold up here anyway.
lines.note_fr: « To hold up » = tenir (devant un juge). « At the table » = à la table des négociations.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: So what am I telling the board? Give me a date.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Announce in early March, authority's decision by end of June, first exits in July. That's tight but doable, provided the file is complete on day one.
lines.note_fr: Style télégraphique naturel à l'oral pour énumérer des jalons. « Tight but doable » = serré mais faisable ; « provided » = à condition que.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: July. They're not going to love it.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I know. But I'd rather give you a date we hit than one we miss in front of a judge.
lines.note_fr: « I'd rather ... than ... » : la préférence argumentée. « To hit a date » = tenir une échéance.

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: Fair enough. Put it in a one-pager and I'll take it upstairs.
lines.note_fr: « Fair enough » = soit, c'est entendu. « A one-pager » = note d'une page ; « to take it upstairs » = le porter à la direction.

questions.q: What does Hélène say about the works council's power?
options: It can veto the plan
It cannot block the plan, but the process cannot be skipped
It approves the plan instead of the labor authority
It only has to be informed after the decision
questions.explain_fr: « They can't veto it. But if we skip the process or rush it, the plan gets thrown out » : pas de veto, mais une étape dont l'irrégularité fait tomber le plan.

questions.q: Why does Hélène reject the idea of paying more and getting releases?
options: Because the budget is already spent
Because the unions would refuse the money
Because money does not shorten the procedure and such a release would not be valid
Because releases are compulsory in France anyway
questions.explain_fr: « Money [...] doesn't buy time. And a release signed before termination wouldn't hold up here » : l'argent n'accélère rien et la renonciation anticipée serait sans valeur.

questions.q: What does 'I'll take it upstairs' mean?
options: I'll present it to senior management
I'll file it in the archives
I'll think it over tonight
I'll send it to the French team
questions.explain_fr: « To take something upstairs » = soumettre à l'échelon supérieur, ici le conseil d'administration.

dialogues.title: Comparing notes with the UK HR director
dialogues.context: Sarah, HR Director for the UK business of the same group, and Hélène are preparing parallel redundancy exercises in Leeds and Angers and compare the two procedures.
dialogues.context_fr: Sarah, DRH de l'activité britannique du même groupe, et Hélène préparent des réductions d'effectifs parallèles à Leeds et à Angers et comparent les deux procédures.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I've got forty-five days pencilled in for the UK side. I take it France will need a little longer?
lines.note_fr: « To pencil in » = prévoir provisoirement. « I take it » = je suppose que. Notez l'euphémisme britannique « a little longer ».

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Rather longer, I'm afraid. We're looking at three months of consultation, and then the authority has to approve the plan.
lines.note_fr: « Rather longer » répond à l'understatement par un autre. « We're looking at » = il faut compter.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Approve it? Goodness. Here we just send the notification form off to the government and get on with consulting the reps.
lines.note_fr: « To get on with » = s'atteler à, poursuivre. Au Royaume-Uni, l'administration est seulement prévenue.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That's the big difference. Your notification is a formality; ours is a decision. Without it, we can't give notice to anyone.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: And do you put people at risk at the start, the way we do?
lines.note_fr: « To put someone at risk » : au Royaume-Uni, informer officiellement un salarié que son poste est menacé.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: No, and that catches everyone out. We announce positions, not names. Individuals only find out once the plan's approved and the selection criteria have been applied.
lines.note_fr: « To catch someone out » = prendre au dépourvu. « To find out » = apprendre, découvrir.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So people sit there for four months not knowing whether it's them? That must be dreadful for morale.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: It's the hardest part, honestly. Which is why we open a voluntary phase early - it takes some of the heat out.
lines.note_fr: « To take the heat out of something » = faire retomber la tension.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: And your selection criteria - can you weight them towards performance? We'd normally score skills, attendance and disciplinary record.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Only up to a point. The law lists the criteria: family circumstances, length of service, age or disability, and professional skills. We can weight them, but we can't leave any of them out.
lines.note_fr: « Only up to a point » = seulement dans une certaine mesure. « To leave out » = écarter, omettre.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Right. So I shouldn't promise the CEO a single European timetable.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I wouldn't. What we can do is line up the announcement dates, so nobody reads about it in the press before they've heard it from us.
lines.note_fr: « I wouldn't » : conseil discret, très britannique. « To line up » = faire coïncider, aligner.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That would be something. Shall we put our two timetables side by side on Thursday?
lines.note_fr: « That would be something » = ce serait déjà cela. « Shall we ...? » : proposition typiquement britannique.

questions.q: What is the main difference Hélène points out about the authorities?
options: In France the authority is only notified
In the UK the government approves the plan
In France the authority must take a decision before notice can be given
Neither country involves the authorities
questions.explain_fr: « Your notification is a formality; ours is a decision » : en France, sans décision de l'administration, aucun licenciement ne peut être notifié.

questions.q: When do individual employees learn that they are affected in France?
options: Once the plan is approved and the criteria have been applied
On the day of the announcement
When they are placed at risk
At the first works council meeting
questions.explain_fr: « Individuals only find out once the plan's approved and the selection criteria have been applied » : on annonce des postes, pas des noms.

questions.q: What can the two HR directors realistically coordinate?
options: The selection criteria
The length of consultation
The severance packages
The announcement dates
questions.explain_fr: « What we can do is line up the announcement dates » : seules les dates d'annonce peuvent être alignées, les procédures restant propres à chaque pays.

dialogues.title: At the negotiating table
dialogues.context: Third negotiation meeting on the plan at the French site of an Indian-owned group. The session is held in English because Rajiv, the group's Chief Restructuring Officer, is attending. Mr Garnier speaks for the majority union.
dialogues.context_fr: Troisième réunion de négociation du plan sur le site français d'un groupe à capitaux indiens. La séance se tient en anglais en raison de la présence de Rajiv, directeur des restructurations du groupe. M. Garnier s'exprime au nom du syndicat majoritaire.

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: Before we go any further, we want one thing on the table. Our members will not accept a single forced departure while the group is paying dividends.
lines.note_fr: « To want something on the table » = vouloir que ce soit posé d'emblée. « Our members » = nos adhérents.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I hear that, Mr Garnier, and we share the aim of keeping compulsory departures as low as we possibly can. That's exactly why we're proposing to open the voluntary phase first.
lines.note_fr: « I hear that » accuse réception sans céder. On reformule l'exigence en objectif commun, sans promettre « zéro ».

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: A voluntary phase at 0.6 of a month per year? Nobody will volunteer for that. It's an insult to people with thirty years' service.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I wouldn't put it quite like that, but I take the point that the figure matters. Can I suggest we park the amount for a moment and look at the package as a whole?
lines.note_fr: « I wouldn't put it quite like that » : désaccord feutré. « I take the point » = j'entends l'argument. « To park » = mettre de côté provisoirement.

lines.speaker: Rajiv
lines.text: If I may - the budget isn't unlimited. But I'm here to listen, and there is some room if it gets us an agreement.
lines.note_fr: « There is some room » = il existe une marge. Ouverture conditionnelle : « if it gets us an agreement ».

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: Then show us. Twelve months' redeployment leave for everyone, not just the over-fifties.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Twelve months across the board is difficult. What we could look at is twelve for the over-fifties and for employees with a disability, and ten for everyone else - if we can agree on the criteria today.
lines.note_fr: « Across the board » = pour tous, sans distinction. « What we could look at is ... if ... » : la formule type de l'offre conditionnelle.

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: You're linking the two.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I am, yes. We need movement on both sides, and I'd rather be open about that than pretend otherwise.
lines.note_fr: Assumer le donnant-donnant : « movement on both sides ». « I'd rather be open about that » renforce la crédibilité.

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: We'll need to take that back to our members. But ten months is not where this ends.
lines.note_fr: « To take something back to » = aller consulter (sa base).

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Understood. Shall we adjourn for half an hour, so you can tell us whether it's a basis for discussion?
lines.note_fr: « To adjourn » = suspendre la séance. « A basis for discussion » = une base de discussion.

lines.speaker: Mr Garnier
lines.text: Half an hour. And bring a better number on the severance.

questions.q: How does Hélène respond to the demand for no forced departures?
options: She promises there will be none
She says the demand is unrealistic
She shares the aim of keeping them as low as possible, without promising zero
She asks Rajiv to answer
questions.explain_fr: Elle dit partager l'objectif (« keeping compulsory departures as low as we possibly can ») sans prendre l'engagement « zéro départ contraint ».

questions.q: What does Hélène offer on redeployment leave?
options: Twelve months for everyone
Twelve months for the over-fifties and disabled employees, ten for the others, linked to agreement on the criteria
Ten months for everyone, with no conditions
Nothing until the severance is agreed
questions.explain_fr: Offre conditionnelle : douze mois pour les plus de cinquante ans et les salariés handicapés, dix pour les autres, « if we can agree on the criteria today ».

questions.q: What does 'park the amount' mean?
options: Increase the amount
Withdraw the amount
Publish the amount
Leave the amount aside for the time being
questions.explain_fr: « To park an issue » = mettre un sujet de côté provisoirement pour avancer sur le reste.

dialogues.title: Briefing the site managers before the announcement
dialogues.context: 7.30 a.m. on announcement day at the Angers plant, which has an international management team. Greg, the American plant director, and Hélène brief the managers; Nadia runs production.
dialogues.context_fr: 7 h 30, le jour de l'annonce, à l'usine d'Angers, dont l'équipe de direction est internationale. Greg, directeur d'usine américain, et Hélène informent les managers ; Nadia dirige la production.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Okay, everybody, thanks for coming in early. What you're about to hear doesn't leave this room until ten o'clock. Hélène, go ahead.
lines.note_fr: « Doesn't leave this room » = reste strictement entre nous. Présent à valeur d'injonction.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Thanks, Greg. At nine this morning we'll tell the works council that the company is proposing to close the Angers finishing line. That would mean cutting 118 positions.
lines.note_fr: « Is proposing » et « would mean » : le vocabulaire du projet, pas de la décision.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Proposing? Come on. It's a done deal, right?
lines.note_fr: « A done deal » = une affaire entendue, pliée.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: It's a proposal, and I need all of you to use that word. Legally, nothing is decided until consultation's over. If we talk like it's final, we hand the unions a lawsuit.
lines.note_fr: « To hand someone a lawsuit » = offrir un procès sur un plateau. « Like it's final » : « like » pour « as if », usage oral américain.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Fine. So what do I tell my guys when they ask if they're on the list?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: The truth: there is no list. The plan names positions, not people, and nobody gets a letter before summer.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: And if they walk out?
lines.note_fr: « To walk out » = débrayer, cesser le travail.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: They might, for a few hours. Don't argue, don't threaten, and don't try to keep the line running at all costs. Safety first, then call me.
lines.note_fr: Trois impératifs négatifs en série : la consigne orale la plus claire. « At all costs » = à tout prix.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: What about the press? There's going to be a TV truck at the gate by noon.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Nobody talks to reporters. Not a word, not even off the record. Send them to the communications team; the number's on your card.
lines.note_fr: « Off the record » = à titre officieux, sans être cité.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: One more thing. You're going to get questions you can't answer. That's okay.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Exactly. Say 'I don't know, but I'll find out,' write it down, and get it to HR today. We'll have answers back to your teams within forty-eight hours.
lines.note_fr: « I don't know, but I'll find out » : la phrase à enseigner aux managers. Ponctuation américaine : la virgule avant le guillemet fermant.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: All right. Let's go do this the right way.
lines.note_fr: « Let's go do » : deux verbes juxtaposés sans « and », tournure américaine.

questions.q: Why does Hélène insist on the word 'proposal'?
options: Because talking as if the decision were final would expose the company legally
Because head office has not yet approved the project
Because the number of positions may increase
Because the press prefers that word
questions.explain_fr: « Legally, nothing is decided until consultation's over. If we talk like it's final, we hand the unions a lawsuit. »

questions.q: What should a manager say to an employee who asks whether he is on the list?
options: That the list will be published at ten o'clock
That HR will tell him tomorrow
That only night-shift staff are concerned
That there is no list, because the plan names positions, not people
questions.explain_fr: « The truth: there is no list. The plan names positions, not people, and nobody gets a letter before summer. »

questions.q: What are managers told to do if journalists approach them?
options: Give the key messages
Speak off the record only
Say nothing and refer them to the communications team
Ask the plant director to answer
questions.explain_fr: « Nobody talks to reporters. Not a word, not even off the record. Send them to the communications team. »

roleplays.title: Explaining to the board why the plan cannot be shortened
roleplays.situation: You are presenting the French restructuring timetable by video to the board of the US parent company. Karen, a board member, pushes for a faster and cheaper process. Explain the French constraints without sounding defensive.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous présentez en visioconférence le calendrier de la restructuration française au conseil d'administration de la maison mère américaine. Karen, administratrice, réclame une procédure plus rapide et moins coûteuse. Expliquez les contraintes françaises sans paraître sur la défensive.

turns.say: Your slide says six months before anyone leaves. In Texas we'd be done in sixty days. Why is France so different?
turns.model: The short answer is that in the US you give notice, whereas in France you have to consult and then get approval. For a plan of this size, the works council has three months to give its opinion, and after that the labor authority must clear the plan before a single letter goes out. Those periods are set by law, so they're not something we can negotiate away.
turns.tips_fr: Commencez par « The short answer is » puis opposez les deux systèmes en une phrase (notice / consult and get approval). « To negotiate away » = faire disparaître par la négociation.

turns.say: What happens if we just go ahead and terminate people on our own schedule?
turns.model: The terminations would be void. Employees could ask a court to put them back in their jobs or award substantial damages, and we'd have to start the whole process again. In practice, cutting corners would cost us more time and far more money than doing it properly.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez la conséquence juridique en un mot (« void »), puis traduisez-la en temps et en argent. « To cut corners » = bâcler, brûler les étapes.

turns.say: And this works council - can't we simply get them to sign off early?
turns.model: They can give their opinion before the deadline if they choose to, but we can't make them. What does help is giving them complete information on day one and agreeing a schedule of meetings with the unions up front. That way three months is the maximum, not the starting point.
turns.tips_fr: Concédez (« they can ... if they choose to »), puis passez à la solution avec « What does help is ». « Up front » = dès le départ.

turns.say: The package looks rich to me. Why are we paying more than the legal minimum?
turns.model: Two reasons. First, the authority checks that the measures are in line with what the group as a whole can afford, not just the French entity, so a bare-minimum plan would probably be rejected. Second, a better package is what gets us a signed agreement with the unions, and an agreement is much harder to challenge in court.
turns.tips_fr: Annoncez la structure (« Two reasons. First, ... Second, ... ») : un conseil d'administration apprécie la clarté. « A bare-minimum plan » = un plan a minima.

turns.say: So what exactly do you need from us today?
turns.model: Three things: approval of the timeline on the slide, a negotiating mandate up to the budget shown, and your agreement that nothing is communicated externally before the works council has been informed. With those, I'm confident we can deliver the plan by July.
turns.tips_fr: Terminez par une demande précise et chiffrable. « I'm confident we can deliver » rassure sans promettre l'impossible.

roleplays.title: Answering a union delegate's objections
roleplays.situation: Negotiation meeting on the plan. Mr Garnier, the delegate of the majority union, challenges the reasons for the plan and the level of the measures. The session is held in English because a group executive is present. Stay calm, acknowledge, and keep the negotiation moving.
roleplays.situation_fr: Réunion de négociation du plan. M. Garnier, délégué du syndicat majoritaire, conteste les raisons du plan et le niveau des mesures. La séance se tient en anglais en raison de la présence d'un dirigeant du groupe. Restez calme, accusez réception et faites avancer la négociation.

turns.say: The group made record profits last year. There is no economic reason for this plan; you are simply moving our jobs to a cheaper country.
turns.model: I understand why it looks that way from here. The group as a whole is profitable, that's true, but the business this plant belongs to has been losing volume for three years, and the figures you've received show that. Your expert will examine them, and we'll answer every question he raises.
turns.tips_fr: Accusez réception (« I understand why it looks that way »), concédez ce qui est exact, puis ramenez aux faits. Renvoyer à l'expert du CSE montre que vous ne craignez pas l'examen.

turns.say: Your figures are your figures. And what you call support measures is the legal minimum with a ribbon on it.
turns.model: I don't think that's quite fair, but I'm not going to defend the first draft line by line. It's a starting point. Tell us which measures matter most to your members, and let's see where we can improve them.
turns.tips_fr: « I don't think that's quite fair » marque le désaccord sans escalade. Transformez l'attaque en question ouverte : « Tell us which measures matter most ».

turns.say: Very well. Our members want a guarantee: no dismissals at all. Volunteers only.
turns.model: I can't give you that guarantee today, and I'd rather be honest about it. What I can commit to is that voluntary departures come first and that we'll review the numbers together before any compulsory step. If we get enough volunteers, the question may not arise.
turns.tips_fr: Refus net mais motivé (« I'd rather be honest »), suivi aussitôt de ce que vous pouvez promettre : « What I can commit to is ... ».

turns.say: And if we refuse to sign? You will write your plan alone and the authority will throw it out.
turns.model: That's a risk for us, I won't deny it. But a unilateral plan would be less generous than what we could agree here, and your members would lose what you've already won at this table. I think we both have more to gain from an agreement.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez le risque (« I won't deny it »), puis montrez le coût du non-accord pour l'autre partie. Concluez sur l'intérêt commun, sans menace.

turns.say: We will see. We want the new proposal in writing before the next meeting.
turns.model: That's reasonable. You'll have a written proposal by Wednesday evening, covering the severance, the length of the leave and the training budget. Shall we keep Friday morning for the next session?
turns.tips_fr: Acceptez, précisez le contenu et l'échéance, puis fixez la suite avec « Shall we ...? ».

roleplays.title: Announcing a site closure to the management team
roleplays.situation: You are announcing to the site's management team, an hour before the works council meeting, that the company is proposing to close the plant. Tom, the logistics manager, reacts strongly. Give clear instructions and deal with the emotion.
roleplays.situation_fr: Une heure avant la réunion du CSE, vous annoncez à l'équipe de direction du site que l'entreprise projette de fermer l'usine. Tom, responsable logistique, réagit vivement. Donnez des consignes claires et accueillez l'émotion.

turns.say: You asked us all to come in at seven. What's going on?
turns.model: Thank you all for coming. I have difficult news. This morning the company will inform the works council that it is proposing to close this site, with production moving to Ghent over the next eighteen months. I wanted you to hear it from me before your teams do.
turns.tips_fr: Annoncez la nouvelle sans détour après une courte phrase de préparation (« I have difficult news »). Gardez « is proposing » : même devant les managers, le projet reste un projet.

turns.say: Close the site? After everything we've done here this year? I don't believe it.
turns.model: I know, Tom. This is a shock, and nothing I say will make it easier. It isn't a judgement on the work you and your teams have done, and I want to be very clear about that. The reasons are about volumes and capacity across Europe, and I'll take you through them in a moment.
turns.tips_fr: Nommez l'émotion (« This is a shock ») avant d'expliquer. Dissociez la décision de la performance des équipes : « It isn't a judgement on the work you have done ».

turns.say: And what about us? Are the managers going as well?
turns.model: All positions at the site are concerned by the proposal, including ours, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I can tell you is that nobody leaves before next year, that redeployment within the group comes first, and that each of you will have an individual conversation with me this week.
turns.tips_fr: Ne minimisez pas : « I won't pretend otherwise ». Enchaînez sur trois certitudes concrètes introduites par « What I can tell you is ».

turns.say: My team's going to ask me a hundred questions at ten o'clock. What am I supposed to say?
turns.model: Stick to three things: it's a proposal, not a decision; nobody will receive a letter before the consultation is over; and the company will support every single person. For anything else, say you don't know yet and that you'll come back to them. You'll have a written Q&A in ten minutes.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez trois messages, pas davantage, et la phrase refuge pour le reste. « Stick to » = tenez-vous-en à.

turns.say: And if they stop work or the press turns up?
turns.model: If people stop work, let them. Don't argue, and make sure the lines are shut down safely. If journalists approach you, say nothing and refer them to the communications team. And call me straight away; I'll be on site all day.
turns.tips_fr: Consignes brèves à l'impératif. « To turn up » = arriver, se présenter. « To refer someone to » = renvoyer vers.

roleplays.title: Handling questions from a journalist and a local official
roleplays.situation: The afternoon after the announcement of the proposed closure, you take a call from Emma, a reporter on an English-language business news service, and then from Mr Baudry, the mayor's chief of staff, who prefers to speak English with the group's representatives. Stay factual and on message.
roleplays.situation_fr: L'après-midi suivant l'annonce du projet de fermeture, vous prenez l'appel d'Emma, journaliste d'un service d'information économique anglophone, puis celui de M. Baudry, directeur de cabinet du maire, qui préfère parler anglais avec les représentants du groupe. Restez factuelle et fidèle aux messages convenus.

turns.say: Emma here, from the business desk. Can you confirm that you're closing the plant and making three hundred people redundant?
turns.model: What I can confirm is that the company presented a proposal to its works council this morning concerning the future of the site. It is a proposal, and it's now subject to consultation with the employee representatives. I'm not in a position to go into the figures while that process is under way.
turns.tips_fr: Ne reprenez pas les mots de la journaliste (« closing », « redundant »). « What I can confirm is » et « I'm not in a position to » encadrent la réponse sans dire « no comment ».

turns.say: Our sources say production is moving abroad to cut costs. Is this about cheaper labour?
turns.model: I won't comment on speculation. The reasons for the proposal have been set out in detail to the employee representatives, and they are the first people we owe explanations to. What I can say is that our priority is to find a solution for every employee concerned.
turns.tips_fr: « I won't comment on speculation » est la formule consacrée. Revenez ensuite à votre message clé avec « What I can say is ».

turns.say: Mr Baudry speaking. The mayor learned about this from the radio. That is not acceptable. Why were we not told first?
turns.model: I quite understand the mayor's frustration, Mr Baudry, and I'm sorry he heard it that way. By law we had to inform the works council before anyone else, which is why we couldn't call you earlier. Our site director tried to reach the mayor's office at ten, and we'd very much like to meet him this week.
turns.tips_fr: Excusez-vous de la manière dont il l'a appris, pas de la décision. Expliquez la contrainte légale (le CSE d'abord) et proposez tout de suite un rendez-vous.

turns.say: This town depends on your factory. What is the group going to do for the area?
turns.model: We're very conscious of what the site means to the town. If the proposal goes ahead, we will look actively for a buyer for the site, and the group will contribute to creating new jobs locally, as French law requires and as we would want to in any case. We'd like to work on that with the mayor and the State's representatives from the start.
turns.tips_fr: Gardez le conditionnel : « If the proposal goes ahead ». Citez les deux obligations (recherche d'un repreneur, revitalisation) en termes simples, sans jargon juridique.

turns.say: The mayor will want commitments in writing, not words.
turns.model: That's entirely fair. I'd suggest we meet on Thursday with our site director, and we'll bring a written note on the timetable and on the commitments we can make at this stage. I'll confirm the time with your office this afternoon.
turns.tips_fr: « That's entirely fair » valide la demande. Proposez une date, un format et une suite précise : la crédibilité passe par le concret.

functional.function: Explaining a French legal constraint to head office
functional.function_fr: Expliquer une contrainte juridique française au siège

phrases.text: Under French law, no dismissal may be notified until the plan has been cleared by the labour authority.
The short answer is no, and here's why.
The closest thing you have to this in the States is a WARN notice, but it goes a good deal further.
It's not that we don't want to move faster; the timetable is set by statute.
If we skip that step, the whole plan can be thrown out.
There's no way around it, I'm afraid, but there are ways to make it shorter.
Think of it as a permit: no approval, no terminations.
The consequence of non-compliance would be the nullity of the dismissals.

functional.function: Keeping to the language of a proposal during consultation
functional.function_fr: S'en tenir au vocabulaire du projet pendant la consultation

phrases.text: The company is proposing to reorganise the site; no decision has been taken.
If the project goes ahead, around sixty positions would be affected.
At this stage, this is a proposal, and it's subject to consultation.
I can't tell you who would be concerned, because nobody knows yet.
The contemplated measures remain subject to the opinion of the works council.
Nothing is set in stone until the consultation is over.
What I can confirm is that a proposal was presented to the works council this morning.
I'd rather not speculate; I'll come back to you as soon as I have a firm answer.

functional.function: Making a conditional offer and trading concessions
functional.function_fr: Faire une offre conditionnelle et échanger des concessions

phrases.text: We could consider moving on the length of the leave, provided we reach agreement on the criteria.
If you can move on that, we can move on this.
What we could look at is twelve months for the over-fifties.
Shall we park that point for now and come back to it?
That's as far as my mandate goes; beyond that, I'd have to go back to head office.
I take your point, but we need movement on both sides.
Let's not let this one issue sink the whole deal.
Management's proposal is made as a package and remains open for signature until Friday.
